findings.title: A j turning angle is read as a float with no bound: the turn is rounded, and an angle of 400 digits gives NaN, which T10 then writes into the address bar and into Copy link as a link that cannot be read
findings.location: site/src/lib/urlCodec.ts:238 (PROJECTION accepts -?\d+ of any length); site/src/components/draw/projector.ts:250-273 (parseProjection Number(m[6..8]); formatProjection writes ((t % 360) + 360) % 360); site/src/components/tools/t10/studio.ts:76-83 (admit stores the formatted text)
findings.claim: The angles of j pass the codec at any length and are parsed with Number. A value beyond 2^53 is rounded, and one beyond about 10^308 becomes Infinity, so formatProjection writes 'NaN'. T10 shows another turn than the link names, and the link it then writes cannot be read.
findings.expected: SPEC 6.6: j takes 'three whole numbers of degrees', and a link opens what it names, or else 'a known key with a value that does not parse' gives the default state with the notice. SPEC 7.4: 'Copy link always encodes the current state'. A link that decodes with no notice must produce a link that decodes to the same state (attack 23).
findings.observed: /tools/geometry/?j=xyz:1,2,3@9007199254740993,0,0 shows no notice and data-out turn '32, 0, 0', but 2^53+1 = 33 mod 360. The bar is rewritten to j=xyz:1,2,3@32,0,0. ?j=xyz:1,2,3@99999999999999999999999,0,0 (279 mod 360) also shows 32. /tools/geometry/?j=xyz:1,2,3@<400 nines>,0,0 shows no notice, data-out projection 'xyz:1,2,3@NaN,0,0', bar ?z=1&g=A3&r=1.0.1&j=xyz:1,2,3@NaN,0,0&e=p, and Copy link gives the same URL. Opening that URL gives the notice. Unit: admit(decodeState(q)) gives projection 'xyz:1,2,3@32,0,0' and 'xyz:1,2,3@NaN,0,0'.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus commit c365fa0 of this branch: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-04-p4-links.test.ts -t 'j angle' (2 failing). Browser: npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/RT-04/playwright.p4.config.ts redteam-RT-04-p4-findings.spec.ts -g 'finding 1' (2 failing).
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 6.6, j row of the value table and Validation ('a known key with a value that does not parse'); SPEC.md 7.4 History API ('Copy link always encodes the current state'); RT-04 attacks 11 and 23
findings.proposedFix: Bound the angle text in the codec (for example at most 9 digits, or reduce the decimal digits mod 360 exactly with BigInt) so that a valid j always gives a finite whole angle. Refuse anything else as a value that does not parse.

findings.title: Opening a valid link rewrites the address bar with replaceState before the reader acts (T10, T11, and T1, T4, T5, T6, T15, T16)
findings.location: site/src/components/board/ToolFrame.svelte:99-110 (registerInstance takes the toolState of the moment as initial, then every later change goes through stateChanged); site/src/components/tools/T10GeometryStudio.svelte:535-550 (the link is applied in a task after hydration); site/src/components/tools/T11FoldingBench.svelte:221-235
findings.claim: ToolFrame registers the instance before the tool has applied its link. The link's state then reaches history.ts through stateChanged as if the reader had changed it, so 500 ms after load the bar is rewritten, normalised, and on lesson pages written for an instance the reader never touched.
findings.expected: Plan, P1-A2 instruction 5.6: 'Nothing is written on load or hydration; the address bar changes only after the reader acts.' Its fragment decisions/P1-A2.md: 'initial the state shown now; registering writes nothing'. SPEC 7.4: replaceState 'after a move'. SPEC 6.6: 'only instances the reader has changed are written'.
findings.observed: With no action, one replaceState about 0.7 to 1.5 s after load. /tools/geometry/?r=1.0.0 becomes ?z=1&g=A3&r=1.0.0&j=xyz:1,2,3@20,30,0&e=p. /tools/geometry/?j=xyz:1,2,3@370,0,0 becomes ...j=xyz:1,2,3@10,0,0... /tools/fold/?g=A5 becomes ?z=1&g=A5&v=n&c=n&s=1,1,1,1,1&w=&y=5.4.3.2.1. /modules/m7-geometry/?b1.r=0.1 becomes ?b1.z=1&b1.g=A2&b1.r=0.1&b1.j=coxeter&b1.e=p. The same happens on /tools/board/, /tools/lab/, /tools/affine/, /tools/sandbox/, /tools/numbers/ and /tools/mirror/. It does not happen on /tools/garden/, /tools/kostant/, /tools/form/, /tools/symbolic/ or /tools/weyl/, which apply the link before registering. Combined with P4-RT-04-01, this write puts '@NaN' into the bar of a reader who only opened a link.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus commit c365fa0: npm ci --prefer-offline; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/RT-04/playwright.p4.config.ts redteam-RT-04-p4-findings.spec.ts -g 'finding 3' (10 failing; each prints the replaceState call and the new bar).
findings.specRef: build-plan/agents/P1-A2-site-infra.md 5.6 ('Nothing is written on load or hydration') (plan); decisions/P1-A2.md registerInstance entry; SPEC.md 7.4 History API; SPEC.md 6.6 'only instances the reader has changed are written'; RT-04 attack 21
findings.proposedFix: Let a tool that applies a link after hydration record it without a write: register with the link's state as initial, or add a history.ts call that sets the recorded state and its defaults comparison without scheduling replaceState. Extend history.test.ts 'nothing is written on load' to a link.

findings.title: T10 prints its squared edge lengths from floating-point measurements: from rings of four digits the values are wrong, and edges of one length are listed as several
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/t10/uniform.ts:84-107 (baseEdgeLengths measures |y0 - y1|^2 in floats; lengthText rounds to 6 decimals; distinctLengths compares those texts); site/src/components/tools/T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1018-1020 (data-out edgeLengths and its data-count)
findings.claim: The squared length of the base edge at a ringed node i is 2 d_i a_i^2, an integer (uniform.ts header; SPEC 2.14). T10 computes it from drawn float coordinates and prints it to 6 decimals as if exact. Float error passes 1e-6 once the value passes about 10^9, so the printed values are wrong, and equal lengths print as different ones. This happens for rings a reader can type or link, at most RING_MAX = 999999.
findings.expected: On A3 with equal rings every edge has one squared length: for (1306,1306,1306) one value 3411272 (data-count 1); for (999999,999999,999999) one value 1999996000002. On G2 (999999,999999) the values are 1999996000002 and 5999988000006. SPEC 5.1 E-1: floating point only in the geometry functions, and a value shown as a number must be that number. SPEC 4.0 Long numbers: a value above 12 digits is shortened, with the exact digits in table, tooltip and export.
findings.observed: /tools/geometry/?r=1306.1306.1306 shows data-out edgeLengths '3411271.999999, 3411272' with data-count 2, while make uniform says 'not needed'. ?r=999999.999999.999999 shows '1999996000001.7036, 1999996000002.15, 1999996000002.1504' with data-count 3. G2 (999999,999999) gives 1999996000001.9995 and 5999988000005.995. The smallest equal ring that already prints several lengths: A3 1306, E8 2220, A8 8883, D4 14017, E6 15945.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus commit c365fa0: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-04-p4-lengths.test.ts (3 failing). Browser: npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/RT-04/playwright.p4.config.ts redteam-RT-04-p4-findings.spec.ts -g 'finding 4' (2 failing).
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 2.14 (squared length a_i^2 (alpha_i, alpha_i)); SPEC.md 5.1 E-1; SPEC.md 4.0 Long numbers; decisions/P4-A3.md 'make uniform' (claims the lengths agree with 2 d_i a_i^2 within 1e-9)
findings.proposedFix: Compute the start's squared lengths exactly as 2 d_i a_i^2 from the symmetrizer (integers, or a_i^2 times the exact norm when uniform is off) and compare those values. Use the float measurement only for the uniform picture, rounded to the precision it actually has.

notes: Attack 10, g=A12 on /tools/board: handled as in round 1 (rerun of the round 1 nodecap and validation tests); nothing new in phase 4.

Attack 11 and 29 grammar notes on the new keys. r=01.0.0 and j=xyz:01,2,3 are accepted and written back as r=1.0.0 and j=xyz:1,2,3 (leading zeros; P4-A2 records them for j). Negative and large angles are normalised: @-30 is written back as @330 and @370 as @10. j=coxeter@90,0,0 on A2 is accepted and drawn flat (P4-A2: on rank 2 only the third angle acts). A ring above RING_MAX = 999999 (r=1000000.0.0) is a valid 6.6 value that T10 refuses with the notice plus its own reason. P4-A3 records this cap; 6.6 does not list it among the failures, so the owner may want to confirm it.

Attack 30, keys of other tools: on /tools/geometry/, w, x, t, y, k, q, d and c=n are decoded into the state with no notice; T10's admit drops them and they are not written back. v=p&m=l and s without c on /tools/geometry/ give the notice through rules 11 and 12, although T10 has no view, mode or start. On a T1 instance, a foreign key such as b1.r=1.0 is kept in the decoded state, so T1's loadFromOutside compares it with the defaults and withdraws an open prediction although the board shows the configured state (code reading, T01GameBoard.svelte:256-258). The specification does not settle foreign keys.

Attack 35 on T10: a link with only g keeps the configured projection when it applies (g=E8 on /tools/geometry/ opens E8 in xyz:1,2,3@20,30,0, not the rank-8 default coxeter), as 6.6 'absent keeps the configured value' and P4-A3 say. The picker instead resets it to the default of the rank. This is a reading for the owner.

Attack 39: T11's preset average is a state object whose tab is not in the link (MERGE accepted this deviation). The average link opens the fold tab. T11 also ignores a parseable m (MERGE accepted the plan rules).

Attack 22: T10 shows a ring edit on the ring board at once, but its link holds the previous rings until the edit's facts are computed. Measured lag here is under 50 ms on E8, inside the 100 ms margin.
Attack 21 timings inside the margin: on T10 and T11 one replaceState arrived 493 to 503 ms after the last of 30 edits.
Attack 28: T10 has no moves. A T10 link whose orbit needs the worker waits for Draw the orbit and starts no worker on load (checked on E8 (1,0,...,0)).
Attack 42: instance ids are unique on every built lesson (94 instances on M0 to M7). The id grammar is from round 1.
